The user asked, in their own words: "is it worth... creating a styling engine or something like that. I want to beef up the kodely engine skills." This is intentionally vague — your job is to figure out what a concrete, buildable "styling engine" could actually mean for THIS codebase specifically, and assess whether it's worth building, not to design the whole thing yet.

Context you need first: read lib/agent.ts in full (the system prompt the builder model receives — note it may be mid-edit by another process working on font/design-plan changes right now; read whatever is currently there, don't worry about catching it at a "final" state), lib/assets/ (the existing ~460-item decorative-asset catalogue and its `find_assets` search tool), lib/foundation.ts (how a new project's starting file tree is seeded), and lib/build-site.ts (the Vite build pipeline).

Investigate and report back on:
1. Right now, does Kodely have ANY reusable, named concept of a "visual style" beyond individual decorative assets (a gradient here, an icon there)? Or is every build's visual identity invented fresh from prose instructions with no persistent, nameable, reusable unit larger than a single asset?
2. What would it concretely mean to build a layer ABOVE the current asset catalogue — e.g., a library of complete, named "look profiles" (each bundling: a palette, a font pairing from the new vendored set, a set of preferred component-styling conventions like card treatment/button shape/spacing rhythm, and a bias toward certain asset categories) that the model picks from and adapts, rather than improvising the whole visual system from scratch on every single build? Is this a realistic, scoped thing to build on top of what already exists, or would it require an architecture change?
3. Is there a natural home for this in the existing codebase's patterns (e.g., could it live in lib/assets/ as a new category, the same way gradients/patterns/icons already do, searched via a variant of `find_assets`)?
4. What's the actual engineering cost/risk here — is this mostly prompt-engineering and data curation (low risk, incremental), or does it require real pipeline changes (e.g., a new pre-generation "pick a look profile" step, new tool definitions for the model, changes to how lib/agent.ts's system prompt is assembled)?
5. Give an honest recommendation on priority: is this worth building now, as a natural next step after the font/design-plan work already in flight, or is it premature until that simpler fix has been evaluated for real impact first?

Report in a clear structured format — findings, then your recommendation. Do not edit any files; this is research only.

The breakpoint is the 608 // difference between the foundation idea working and being a net loss. 609 // 610 // Below the model's minimum cacheable prefix the breakpoint is ignored 611 // rather than erroring, so a tiny project is unaffected. 612 messages.push({ 613 role: "user", 614 content: [{ type: "text", text: requestText, cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" } }], 615 }); 616 } 617 618 const totals = { 619 inputTokens: 0, 620 outputTokens: 0, 621 cacheReadTokens: 0, 622 cacheWriteTokens: 0, 623 }; 624 625 // Bounded so a confused model can never bill the user for an endless loop. 626 const MAX_TURNS = 8; 627 628 for (let turn = 0; turn < MAX_TURNS; turn++) { 629 if (opts.signal?.aborted) return; 630 631 const stream = anthropic.messages.stream( 632 { 633 model, 634 max_tokens: 32_000, 635 thinking: { type: "adaptive" }, 636 output_config: { effort }, 637 system: [{ type: "text", text: SYSTEM, cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" } }], 638 tools: TOOLS, 639 messages, 640 }, 641 { signal: opts.signal }, 642 ); 643 644 for await (const event of stream) { 645 if (event.type === "content_block_delta" && event.delta.type === "text_delta") { 646 yield { type: "text", text: event.delta.text }; 647 } 648 } 649 650 const message = await stream.finalMessage(); 651 totals.inputTokens += message.usage.input_tokens ?? 0; 652 totals.outputTokens += message.usage.output_tokens ?? 0; 653 totals.cacheReadTokens += message.usage.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0; 654 totals.cacheWriteTokens += message.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0; 655 656 if (message.stop_reason === "refusal") { 657 throw new Error( 658 "The request was declined. Try describing the site you want in different terms.", 659 ); 660 } 661 662 const toolUses = message.content.filter( 663 (b): b is Anthropic.ToolUseBlock => b.type === "tool_use", 664 ); 665 666 if (toolUses.length === 0) { 667 yield { type: "usage", model, ...totals }; 668 return; 669 } 670 671 messages.push({ role: "assistant", content: message.content }); 672 673 const results: Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam[] = []; 674 for (const use of toolUses) { 675 const input = use.input as { 676 path?: string; 677 content?: string; 678 query?: string; 679 kind?: string; 680 limit?: number; 681 }; 682 683 // Handled before the path check below — this is the one tool that takes 684 // no path, and running it through normalizePath would reject it outright. 685 if (use.name === "find_assets") { 686 yield { type: "progress", text: "Picking out icons and artwork" }; 687 const matches = findAssets(input.query ?? "", { 688 kind: input.kind as AssetKind | undefined, 689 limit: Math.min(Math.max(input.limit ?? 6, 1), 12), 690 }); 691 results.push({ 692 type: "tool_result", 693 tool_use_id: use.id, 694 content: formatMatchesForTool(matches), 695 }); 696 continue; 697 } 698 699 const path = normalizePath(input.path ?? ""); 700 701 if (!path) { 702 results.push({ 703 type: "tool_result", 704 tool_use_id: use.id, 705 content: `Rejected: '${input.path}' is not a valid project-relative path.`, 706 is_error: true, 707 }); 708 continue; 709 } 710 711 // Narrate before applying, so the line appears while the write is 712 // happening rather than after it lands. 713 const line = narrateTool(use.name, { path }); 714 if (line) yield { type: "progress", text: line }; 715 716 if (use.name === "write_file") { 717 const ok = await opts.onWrite(path, input.content ?? ""); 718 if (ok) yield { type: "file", path, action: "write" }; 719 results.push({ 720 type: "tool_result", 721 tool_use_id: use.id, 722 content: ok ? `Wrote ${path}.` : `Could not write ${path}.`, 723 is_error: !ok, 724 }); 725 } else if (use.name === "delete_file") { 726 const ok = await opts.onDelete(path); 727 if (ok) yield { type: "file", path, action: "delete" }; 728 results.push({ 729 type: "tool_result", 730 tool_use_id: use.id, 731 content: ok ? `Deleted ${path}.` : `${path} did not exist.`, 732 is_error: false, 733 }); 734 } else { 735 results.push({ 736 type: "tool_result", 737 tool_use_id: use.id, 738 content: `Unknown tool ${use.name}.`, 739 is_error: true, 740 }); 741 } 742 } 743 744 messages.push({ role: "user", content: results }); 745 } 746 747 yield { type: "usage", model, ...totals }; 748 } 749

1	/**
2	 * The asset library's front door: one catalogue and one query function over
3	 * every inlinable asset Kodely can hand a generated site.
4	 *
5	 * THE SEAM
6	 * {@link findAssets} is deliberately shaped like a tool call. A future agent
7	 * tool ("search_assets") should be able to forward its arguments straight
8	 * through and hand the model back `AssetMatch[]` — each match already carries
9	 * a paste-ready `source` and a one-line `usage`, so the model never has to
10	 * invent SVG geometry or guess at a CSS incantation. Wiring that tool into
11	 * lib/agent.ts is not this module's job; being callable from it is.
12	 *
13	 * WHY EVERY MATCH IS INLINABLE
14	 * Generated sites run under `default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:;
15	 * connect-src 'none'` with no way to add npm packages, so a hosted asset —
16	 * however convenient — would fail silently at serve time. Every `source`
17	 * string here is either markup, CSS, or a `data:` URI, all of which survive
18	 * that sandbox. See the header comments in ./icons.ts and ./patterns.ts.
19	 *
20	 * WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
21	 * Photography. Not "not yet" — there is no host to serve it from, and a base64
22	 * raster would cost more in model context than the rest of a build. Where a
23	 * site would reach for a stock photo it gets ./illustrations.ts instead:
24	 * generated hero backdrops, flat spot drawings, decorative marks and
25	 * empty-state art, all of it geometry.
26	 */
27

92	export type AssetMatch = {
93	  /** Stable, namespaced: "icon:phone", "flag:fr", "gradient:sunset". */
94	  id: string;
95	  kind: AssetKind;
96	  name: string;
97	  keywords: string[];
98	  format: "jsx" | "svg" | "css" | "text";
99	  /** The thing to paste into the generated site. */
100	  source: string;
101	  /** One line telling the caller where this goes. */
102	  usage: string;
103	  /** Alternative representations — raw svg, data URI, Tailwind class, colours. */
104	  variants?: Record<string, string>;

106	  score: number;

109	export type FindAssetsOptions = {

123	
124	type Entry = {
125	  id: string;
126	  kind: AssetKind;
127	  name: string;
128	  /** Lowercased, de-duplicated search terms. */
129	  keywords: string[];

132	
133	function iconEntry(icon: Icon): Entry {
134	  return {
135	    id: `icon:${icon.id}`,
136	    kind: "icon",
137	    name: icon.name,
138	    keywords: icon.keywords,
139	    render: (opts) => ({
140	      format: "jsx",
141	      source: iconJsx(icon.id, { weight: opts.weight ?? "regular", size: null, className: "h-6 w-6" }) ?? "",
142	      usage:
143	        "Paste inline into a .tsx file. Stroke is currentColor, so set the colour with a Tailwind text-* class on the icon or its parent; size with h-*/w-*.",
144	      variants: {
145	        svg: iconSvg(icon.id, { weight: opts.weight ?? "regular" }) ?? "",
146	        dataUri: iconDataUri(icon.id, { weight: opts.weight ?? "regular" }) ?? "",

148	      },

153	// Adjectival forms, as a KEYWORD on the country itself rather than a
154	// query-side synonym.

156	// Why it has to be entry-side: flag keywords are derived from the country
157	// name, so "French Guiana" owns the literal token "french" and scored a full
158	// keyword hit, while France could only be reached through a synonym — which is
159	// deliberately discounted, and is only consulted when the literal token scores
160	// zero. "french flag" therefore returned French Guiana, French Polynesia and
161	// French Southern Territories, and not France. Same for "british" (British
162	// Indian Ocean Territory) and "american" (American Samoa).

165	// the same strength. Territory searches still work, because "french guiana"
166	// carries a second token that only the territory matches.
167	const DEMONYMS: Record<string, string[]> = {

183	  ca: ["canadian"],

203	function flagEntry(flag: Flag): Entry {

207	    ...(DEMONYMS[flag.code] ?? []),

214	    id: `flag:${flag.code}`,
215	    kind: "flag",
216	    name: flag.name,
217	    keywords: kw,
218	    render: (): Rendered => {
219	      const svg = flag.svg ? flagSvg(flag.code, { width: 60 }) : null;
220	      if (svg) {

225	            flag.svg?.accuracy === "simplified"
226	              ? `Hand-authored SVG, JSX-ready. SIMPLIFIED: ${flag.svg.note ?? "detail omitted"} — use the emoji instead if exactness matters.`

682	      a.entry.name.length - b.entry.name.length ||

# Findings: Is a "Styling Engine" Worth Building for Kodely?

## What I read
- `lib/agent.ts` (748 lines, includes uncommitted Records/Accounts backend work — not font-related)
- `lib/assets/index.ts`, `lib/assets/materialize.ts` (catalogue + `find_assets`)
- `lib/foundation.ts` (project seed files)
- `lib/build-site.ts` (Vite build pipeline)
- `lib/brand-kit.ts`, `lib/wizard.ts`, `lib/features.ts` (adjacent systems that turned out highly relevant)
- CSP definition in `app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts`

---

## 1. Does Kodely have any reusable, named "visual style" unit today?

**Almost — one exists, but it's a UI-only artifact, not a builder-time concept.**

`lib/wizard.ts` defines `LOOK_DIRECTIONS`: six named objects (`warm-rustic`, `clean-clinical`, `bold-editorial`, `fresh-natural`, `soft-elegant`, `bright-energetic`), each bundling exactly what a "look profile" would need:
- a resolved `GradientPreset` (palette) from `lib/assets/patterns.ts`
- a `headingFont` (system-stack only), `headingWeight`, `headingTracking`
- a `typography` prose description
- a `density`/`densityLabel` (spacing/layout rhythm)

This is a real, nameable, reusable unit *larger than a single asset*. But its life ends at prompt assembly: `assemblePrompt()` in `lib/wizard.ts` flattens the chosen look into a paragraph of prose (`visualDirection()`) that gets pasted into the textarea a user can edit/delete. The builder model in `lib/agent.ts` never sees `LOOK_DIRECTIONS` as data — it only ever sees whatever prose survived into the final prompt, same as any other line of user text. There's no tool, no catalogue entry, no id the model can look up or ask for more of.

Outside the wizard's 6 pre-baked directions, every build's visual identity is invented fresh from `SYSTEM`'s generic instructions ("Give the page one distinctive visual idea..."), the asset catalogue's individual pieces (one gradient, one icon, one divider at a time), and whatever adjectives are in the user's prompt. `lib/brand-kit.ts` adds a customer's own logo/palette but explicitly has "no typography field... Type is the system stack" — confirmed again in `lib/features.ts`'s `custom-fonts` feature-gap entry: *"The CSP sets no font-src... A base64 font is blocked exactly like a hosted one."* No vendored font pairing system exists yet anywhere in the repo I could find (`grep` for "vendored"/"design plan"/"look profile" turned up nothing outside asset-provenance docs).

So: **there is one half-built precedent (`LOOK_DIRECTIONS`), and it proves the concept but stops one layer short of where the model could use it.**

## 2. What would a layer above the asset catalogue concretely look like — and is it realistic?

Concretely, extending `LOOK_DIRECTIONS` into a real "look profile" catalogue would mean each entry bundling:
- palette (already solved — reuse `GradientPreset` ids, exactly as `LOOK_DIRECTIONS` and `brand-kit.ts` already do)
- font pairing (blocked today — no font-src, no vendoring; this is a prerequisite, not this feature's job)
- component conventions (card radius/shadow, button shape, spacing scale) — currently exists only as prose in `LOOK_DEFS.typography`/`.density`, never as a real convention the model is told to apply consistently across `write_file` calls
- asset-category bias (e.g. "bold-editorial" leans on `divider`/`mark` kinds, "soft-elegant" leans on `illustration`/`gradient`) — doesn't exist at all today; `find_assets` has no awareness of a "current look"

This is realistic to build **on top of** what exists — it is not an architecture change. The asset catalogue (`lib/assets/index.ts`) already has the exact shape for it: an `AssetKind`, an `Entry`, a `render()` function, keyword search via `findAssets()`. A `"look"` kind slots into `ASSET_KINDS` the same way `"gradient"` or `"divider"` did. The hard parts are all curation/design work (choosing 8-15 good profiles, writing their component-convention prose, picking asset biases), not plumbing.

## 3. Is there a natural home in existing patterns?

Yes, directly:
- **As a new `AssetKind`** (`"look"` or `"style"`) in `lib/assets/index.ts`, following the exact pattern gradients/patterns/dividers already use — a data array + a `render()` closure + keywords, folded into `buildCatalog()`.
- **Searched via a variant of `find_assets`** — either the same tool with `kind: "look"`, or a new `pick_look` tool in `TOOLS` in `lib/agent.ts` that returns one profile's full bundle (palette id + font stack + convention notes + biased asset ids) in one call, the same shape `formatMatchesForTool` already produces for other kinds.
- **`lib/wizard.ts`'s `LOOK_DIRECTIONS` becomes the seed data**, not a parallel system — the six existing directions plus more, promoted from wizard-only prose into catalogue entries usable by every build path (composer, wizard, and edits), not just the wizard.

This is the cleanest possible integration point in the codebase — it reuses an established pattern rather than inventing one.

## 4. Engineering cost/risk

Mostly low-risk, but not *purely* prompt engineering — there's one small, well-scoped pipeline change plus curation work:

- **Low-risk (data + prompt work):**
  - Moving `LOOK_DIRECTIONS` (or a superset) into `lib/assets/` as a real catalogue kind — mechanical, same shape as five existing kinds.
  - Writing the component-convention prose per profile (card treatment, button shape, spacing rhythm) — pure content work, no code risk.
  - Biasing `find_assets` results toward a chosen profile's asset categories — a filter/boost, not a new search engine.

- **Real (small) pipeline change:**
  - A new tool definition in `TOOLS` (`lib/agent.ts`) if you want the model to actively *pick* a look rather than just have one handed to it in the prompt (as the wizard does today) — this is a few dozen lines, same shape as `find_assets`'s existing wiring (`normalizePath`-style validation isn't even needed since it takes no path).
  - Deciding *when* the model picks: a pre-generation step (before the main turn) vs. letting it call the tool mid-build like `find_assets`. The latter is basically free — same loop, same `messages.push` pattern already in `runAgent`. A dedicated pre-generation "pick a look profile" step would be new orchestration in `runAgent`/`lib/agent-sdk.ts` and is the one piece that's a genuine (if small) architecture addition.
  - `lib/agent-sdk.ts`'s materialize-to-disk bridge (`lib/assets/materialize.ts`) would need the new kind folded in too, since it mirrors the whole catalogue — trivial, same loop.

- **Not in scope for this feature, but a blocking dependency if "font pairing from the vendored set" is taken literally:** actual web fonts require either (a) a CSP change to add `font-src 'self'` plus vendoring real `.woff2` files as static assets in the build output (`lib/build-site.ts`'s `TEXT_EXTENSIONS` only allows text formats today, so binary font files would need new handling), or (b) staying on system-stack pairings only (e.g., serif-heading/sans-body combos), which needs no infra work at all. The two are separable — a look-profile catalogue can ship with system-stack font pairings today and gain real vendored fonts later without a redesign.

Overall: **incremental and additive, not a rewrite.** The riskiest part is not code, it's curation quality — a shallow set of look profiles that just restates "warm and modern" in different words would add token cost and a new tool round-trip without moving the needle on actual visual variety.

## 5. Recommendation

**Sequence it after the font/vendoring work is evaluated, not before — but scope it now while that's fresh, because it's the natural next step and cheap to plan.**

Reasoning:
- The single highest-leverage unresolved constraint on Kodely's visual range is typography: `custom-fonts` is explicitly listed as unsupported in `lib/features.ts`, and every "look" the wizard offers today is differentiated by palette/density/weight, never by an actual different typeface, because there isn't one available. If the in-flight font/design-plan work makes real font pairings possible, a look-profile catalogue becomes dramatically more valuable overnight — it goes from "6 palettes with prose about density" to "6 genuinely distinct visual identities." Building the look-profile layer first, on system fonts only, means redoing/expanding it the moment fonts land.
- Conversely, if the font work stalls or gets descoped, the look-profile catalogue is still worth doing on its own — `LOOK_DIRECTIONS` already proves users respond to picking a named direction over an adjective, and promoting it from "wizard-only, 6 hardcoded options, flattened to prose" to "first-class catalogue entry, searchable by the model on every build, not just when the wizard was used" is a real improvement to build consistency even without new fonts.
- Priority-wise: this is a "beef up the engine" investment, not an urgent fix — nothing is broken today, and the wizard already gives users *some* of this value in a narrower form. It's reasonable to treat it as the next scoped project once the font work either ships or is confirmed deprioritized, since that determines whether you're curating 6-10 palette-only profiles or a genuinely richer catalogue with real typography — and you don't want to curate the content twice.

**Concrete first step, whenever you pick it up:** promote `LOOK_DIRECTIONS` out of `lib/wizard.ts` into `lib/assets/` as a new `AssetKind`, keep it wizard-compatible (no regression), and only then decide whether the model gets it via a dedicated tool or via the same `find_assets` path with `kind: "look"`.
